name: Florida
headline_status: Medical cannabis is legal for registered patients; recreational use remains illegal.
summary: Florida voters approved a broad medical cannabis program (Amendment 2) in November 2016 with 72% of the vote, and patients buy from licensed Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers. Adult-use legalization (Amendment 3) won 56% in 2024 but fell short of the 60% needed, and a 2026 follow-up failed to qualify for the ballot after the state struck petition signatures and the Florida Supreme Court declined review in March 2026. Possession of up to 20 grams without a card remains a misdemeanor carrying up to a year in jail.

medical_since.value: Amendment 2 approved Nov. 8, 2016 with 72% of the vote; an earlier 2014 law allowed only low-THC cannabis.

medical_program.value: Patients need a qualifying condition, certification from a qualified Florida physician, entry in the Medical Marijuana Use Registry and a registry ID card; they buy from licensed Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers. A 2025 law requires revoking registrations of patients and caregivers convicted of certain drug trafficking or sale offenses.

home_grow.value: Not allowed, including for medical patients; a 2026 bill to permit six plants never got a committee vote.

retail_sales.value: Medical-only, through licensed Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers (MMTCs). No adult-use stores.

regulator.value: Office of Medical Marijuana Use (OMMU), part of the Florida Department of Health.

penalties.value: Possessing up to 20 grams is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in jail and a $1,000 fine; more than 20 grams is a felony with up to five years and a $5,000 fine. Some cities and counties allow civil citations instead.

hemp_thc.value: Hemp-derived THC products are widely sold with light regulation; Gov. DeSantis vetoed a 2024 bill that would have banned many of them.

ballot_history.value: Amendment 3 (2024 adult-use) won 56% but needed 60%. The 2026 Smart & Safe Florida initiative failed to qualify after signatures were struck; the Florida Supreme Court declined review in March 2026.

timeline.event: Compassionate Medical Cannabis Act allows low-THC cannabis
Voters approve Amendment 2 creating the full medical program
Gov. DeSantis vetoes a bill restricting hemp-derived THC products
Adult-use Amendment 3 gets 56%, short of the 60% required
SB 2514 signed, requiring registry revocation for patients convicted of certain drug offenses
1st District Court of Appeal lets the state disqualify 2026 initiative signatures
Florida Supreme Court declines review; adult-use measure stays off the 2026 ballot

faq.a: Only for registered medical patients. Recreational use is illegal; a 2024 legalization amendment fell short of the 60% needed, and a 2026 attempt did not make the ballot.

faq.q: How do you get a medical marijuana card in Florida?
faq.a: See a qualified Florida physician who certifies a qualifying condition, get entered in the state's Medical Marijuana Use Registry, then apply for a registry ID card through the Office of Medical Marijuana Use.

faq.q: What is the penalty for weed possession in Florida?
faq.a: Up to 20 grams is a misdemeanor with up to a year in jail and a $1,000 fine. More than 20 grams is a felony. Some localities issue civil citations instead.

faq.q: Can you grow cannabis at home in Florida?
faq.a: No. Home cultivation is not allowed, even for medical patients.

faq.q: Will Florida vote on recreational marijuana in 2026?
faq.a: No. The 2026 initiative failed to qualify after the state disqualified signatures and the Florida Supreme Court declined to hear the campaign's challenge in March 2026.
